headline: Ward 47's best ranks are about the neighborhood. Its worst ranks are about paperwork.
summary:
Ward 47's best ranks point to one kind of place. Households here connect to broadband at the highest rate in Chicago, area schools post the top share of students meeting state proficiency standards, residents report the strongest sense of belonging to their neighborhood, and no other ward has more licensed child care per resident. None of those four numbers measure the same thing directly, but together they read the way indicators of a settled, resourced residential population usually do.

The ward's worst ranks tell a different kind of story. Menu money spent on street and alley lighting lands at 49th, but the gap between wards on this measure is thin enough that thirty-eight of them crowd inside a two-point band, so the specific rank says more about this year's budget ledger than about which blocks are lit. The demolition-permit count lands at 48th because Ward 47 has one of the highest counts in the city on a measure where fewer permits score better, and that count is climbing for a visible reason right now. Developers secured a permit this month to tear down the shuttered Torstenson Glass factory in Lake View for a 99-unit apartment building, the kind of teardown that raises this number in a ward people are still trying to build in.
reading_the_rankings: Ward 47's rank of 49th for grocery stores reads like a food desert, but the measure only counts businesses licensed specifically as a grocery store per 10,000 residents, so a ward built around a handful of large supermarkets rather than many small shops will always show a thin count here, a business-classification artifact rather than an account of where people actually buy food. The school numbers invite a similar misread. Per-pupil spending ranks 49th while the same schools rank 1st for the share of students meeting state proficiency standards, one a CPS budget line and the other a test outcome, two figures that were never going to move together and that this dataset never tries to connect.

news.headline: Chicago's first-ever 'cat tour' brings a day of whimsy to Lincoln Square: 'I think people need it'
news.note: Lincoln Square hosted Chicago's first cat-themed walking tour, pairing more than 125 residents' cats along four routes with a cat video festival benefiting local rescues.

news.headline: Lake View's former Torstenson Glass building will be demolished, replaced by luxury apartments
news.note: Developers secured demolition permits for the former Torstenson Glass manufacturing building at 3233 N. Sheffield Ave. and plan a 99-unit apartment building in its place.

news.headline: Woman killed in Lake View hit-and-run crash
news.note: A 25-year-old pedestrian died after a driver struck her while she crossed Irving Park Road and fled the scene, causing further collisions before being caught.

news.headline: Ann Sather moving into shuttered Stella's Diner in Lake View
news.note: The longtime Chicago restaurant chain bought the closed Stella's Diner space at 3042 N. Broadway to open a new location there.
